items.instruction: Match the correct ending to the beginning of these sentences.
items.title: Classify that!
items.body:
Although the phrase 'medical device' may conjure images of intensive care units	
the truth is that many of the products you use every day are also considered medical devices by regulatory bodies.

Toothbrushes, bandages, and latex gloves	
are all examples of low-risk medical devices.

Pregnancy tests, powered wheelchairs, and contact lenses on the other hand	
are considered intermediate-risk devices and are subject to more regulatory controls.

Implants like pacemakers and artificial joints, and life-sustaining equipment like high-frequency ventilators	
are clearly more critical and are classified as high-risk.

Each regulatory authority has different criteria and regulations	
so classifications of specific devices vary around the world.

items.instruction: Read this story and highlight all the past continuous tenses.
items.title: What a day!
items.body: Last Monday was the worst day of my life! You know I got a part in a film, right? Well, I was learning my lines when the doorbell rang. It was my neighbor. She was crying like a baby. Well, I invited her in. I mean, what else could I do? While I was making her tea, her friend arrived. And after about a minute, they were shouting at each other. 'You stole my part!' she screamed. 'I didn't get the part either,' my neighbor yelled back. Then the friend began to quote some lines. 'Where were you when our father was dying?' I froze and looked down at the script in my hand. 'I was crying my eyes out,' I whispered.

Kenya is regarded by many as the 'Jewel of East Africa' and has some of the continent's finest beaches, most interesting wildlife and stunning scenery. It is a startlingly beautiful land, from the coral reefs and white sand beaches of the coast to the summit of Mount Kenya.
Between these two extremes is the rolling savannah that is home to game parks, the highlands with their green fields of coffee and tea plantations, and the most spectacular stretch of the Great Rift Valley.
Kenya also has a fascinatingly diverse population with around 40 tribes, all with their own language and culture. Of them all, however, the most famous are the beautiful red-dressed Masai, who still lead a traditional lifestyle.

items.body:
Rock and roll emerged as a defined musical style in the United States in the late 1940s, when it was called rhythm and blues. The term 'rocking,' which referred to dancing, also had a hidden sexual meaning. The songs were mostly written by black artists, who were still largely segregated from white society. Therefore, the music never gained great popularity until it broke through the racial and moral boundaries that kept it contained to small audiences.
In the early 1950s, the racial boundary was broken when white musicians began writing 'rock' songs. White teenagers loved the music, but their parents still considered it immoral. It continued to gain in popularity and over time, the moral objections diminished. However, it continues to be a musical genre that pushes the limits and often creates heated opposition.

items.body: The World Bank comprises two : the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). The IBRD's original  was to  the reconstruction of nations devastated by WWII. Today, its mission has expanded to fighting . It provides  to governments and public enterprises. Its  comes primarily from the world's financial markets. The IDA focuses on helping the world's poorest countries. It provides interest-free loans, grants and  with repayment periods of between 35 and 40 years. Most of the IDA's funding comes from contributions made by  member countries. IDA funding is directed primarily at primary , basic health , clean water , environmental safeguards, and institutional and infrastructural . The aim of these projects is to lead the way to economic , job , higher  and better living conditions.

items.body:
unobtrusive
	Like tools, products should fulfill a purpose. Good design should be neutral and restrained.

long-lasting
	It avoids fashion and therefore never appears out-of-date.

honest
	Good design doesn't pretend to be more innovative or powerful than it really is.

innovative
	Good design always develops in tandem with technology, and can never be an end in itself.

thorough
	Nothing is arbitrary or left to chance. Good design considers every last detail.

useful
	A product is bought to be used. Good design emphasizes the usefulness of a product and disregards anything that could detract from it.

environmentally friendly
	Good design uses resources responsibly throughout its life cycle.

simple
	Less is more. Good design focuses on the essential.

understandable
	A well-designed product is self-explanatory.

aesthetic

items.body:
Who are the Generation Y'ers and how 
are they changing
 the way we work? Generation Y, born anytime between the late 1970s and 2000, is a new breed. They have been pampered, nurtured and fed on a diet of wide-ranging extracurricular activities.  They've grown up questioning their parents and now 
they're doing
 the same to their employers. Generation Y 
doesn't respond
 well to a command-and-control style of management; they prefer to collaborate. They seek environments where creativity and independent thinking is a prerequisite. Gen Y'ers don't tend to look for one long assignment; they want change. This is a generation of multitaskers; they juggle email on their tablets while chatting on smartphones.  And they 
feel
 completely at home in a virtual world.
Generation Y'ers are not just independent and technically savvy, they 
belong
 to a post-9-11 era. They 
want
 a life and they want their jobs to fit into this picture. They demand flexibility, telecommuting options and the possibility to go part-time – or leave the workforce temporarily – when children are in the picture.  And they 
see
 the full financial picture. Half of all Gen Y'ers 
factor in
 a company's retirement benefits package into their job choices. | are they changing

items.body:
20th century corporate structures focused on 
vertical
 organization. A large corporation's organization chart would typically show several 
tiers
 of managers, with decision-making 
flow
 moving from top to bottom. This model emphasized job 
specialization
, formal procedures and protocols, and it 
centralized
 authority and accountability.
Recently, however, corporations have moved away from this model: One approach has been to switch to 
flat
 hierarchies. In some companies, this has involved extracting several layers of 
middle
 management. The effect was positive.  The 
streamlined
 organization not only saved on personnel costs, but improved communication and decision making.
Technology has also had a flattening effect: Intranets, social networking software and wikis have made information readily available.  Meetings take place virtually and are more 
inclusive
. Some companies institute 
self-directed
 work teams as the standard production group. The move aims to de-emphasize job specialization and 
authority
 and facilitate decision making and goal setting at all levels. | vertical

sole proprietorship

general partnership

limited liability partnership

limited liability company

corporation

items.title: Monitoring employee activity
items.body:
More than one-third of the American workforce expects their employer to 
monitor
 their email or even to put them under surveillance on a regular basis. Whether it's gauging employee 
productivity
, complying with 
legal requirements
, ensuring 
data security
 or even fighting corporate 
spying
, companies walk a fine line in the world of workplace 
ethics
.
Where should employers – and employees – draw the line?  Subjecting employees to constant scrutiny may keep the majority on track and catch any 
wrongdoers
, but doing so raises a lot of questions about 
privacy
. Who owns a picture of the family saved on the computer desktop? Is it okay to make personal phone calls during work hours?
The key for company managers is to 
formulate
 a clear policy and make sure employees have not only read it but understood it. Making sure the policy is in keeping with the corporate culture is important, too. A company specializing in web products with a relaxed working environment that suddenly forbids private email usage might have trouble enforcing a strict internet policy. A law firm, which by design is a more conservative workplace, might not.  In any case, if the 
policy
 makes sense, most employees will willingly follow it. | monitor

Indian movie producers and distributors are refusing  release movies to big theater chains  they get a guarantee of 50 percent of the revenue from ticket sales  all movies for the first four weeks of their .
The dispute, which has been simmering  years, is coming to a boil at a difficult time for Indian movies. The country's big Hindi-language film industry,  as Bollywood, has not produced a big hit in the last three months. -office revenue fell 2.3  in the first quarter from sales in the period a year earlier, to 2.6 billion rupees, or $52 million, according to IBOS, a film-industry news service.
Filmmakers assert that an across-the- revenue split would cripple theater chains because most of the hundreds of movies released every year do not earn much money. items.title: Chocolate-covered insects
items.body:
A bright, engaging man, Mr Van Dongen, who is head of the meat department at Sligro, a kind of Costco on the edge of this trim Dutch town. Besides to steaks, poultry and other kinds of meat, he offers mealworms, buffalo worms, locusts and other insects, as well as prepared products which containing insects like Bugs Sticks and Bugs Nuggets – not for pets, but as a source of protein for people.
On a recent afternoon he furthermore arranged two sample stands, one with chunks of chocolate laced with ground mealworms (larvae for a type of beetle), yet another with various kinds of whole insects for munching, despite including worms and crickets, in small plastic containers.
At a nearby stand with such a Dutch name that translated roughly as the Tasting Garden, there were more insects than garden. While shoppers gazed with puzzled looks, Mr Van Dongen, 41, warmed up portions of an Asian vegetable dish with crickets mixed in.

items.title: Future famine?
items.body:
In 1968, when the world's population was around 3.7 billion, the American Assembly met to talk about what could be done to head off a potential 
global food
 crisis by the year 2000. The expectation was that the population would double by the millennium.  The number of 
malnourished
 people – estimated to affect about 37 percent of the world's 
population
 in 1970 – was expected to rise as well.
How could governments and global agencies best assist the starving and avoid 
famine
? The Assembly concluded that the US should increase foreign aid and that developing countries should expand birth control measures.  It also recommended encouraging investment by private corporations specializing in 
agricultural
 products and 
food processing
.
Today, the global population is believed to have reached 7 billion.  While the percentage of the population that is 
starving
 has dropped since the 1970s to about 13 percent, rates remain distressingly high. Even with monetary aid and improved crop 
yields
, which are attributed to better 
seed
 stock and farming equipment, an estimated 925 million people still don't get enough to eat. Conversely, in the United States alone, 62 percent of the adult population is 
overweight
 or 
obese
, a number that has doubled since 1970.
Now scientists and organizations are beginning to consider how the world will cope with the estimated 10 billion who may be living on our planet by the year 2100.  How can we make farming more 
sustainable
 and effective? Did any of the measures proposed in 1970 actually help curb hunger? What new methods are available to us now? What new possibilities might work in the future? | global food

items.title: Feedback form
items.body:
'I called up Laptop World when I spilled coffee on my keyboard. I would describe the service I got there as being moderately competent. The customer service representative was quite pleasant, and even patient, but he had to ask for help to solve the problem. When he did give me a response, I have to say that I didn't have any confidence in it. I don't think I would return to Laptop World again.' Janet Doe
'I'm not the type to go off in a tizzy over unenthusiastic customer service. I try to be a little understanding, too. After all, it can't be easy listening to people's problems and complaints every day for 8 hours. I don't think it's right to be too strict with the person. Instead, I try to direct my aggression to the item in question; in my case, that was my laptop which I spilled coffee over. The service rep did his best to reply, though frankly, I had the feeling he was a little unsure. He might have been new. Anyway, would I buy a laptop there again? Yeah, I mean, if I hadn't knocked over my cup, I wouldn't be talking to you right now.' Jasmin Doe
'I was infuriated by the treatment I received when I called Laptop World. The customer service representative was anything but knowledgeable. And professionalism seemed to have gone out of fashion there, too. I was left hanging on the line for ages and when the representative did eventually take my call, he just blurted out the first inane response that came into his head. I told him that I had spilled coffee on my laptop, and before I could finish my sentence, he insisted I get the hairdryer out and dry it. What I tried to tell him – unsuccessfully – was that the incident had happened a week before and that now a couple of the keys didn't work. But, he was too impatient to get me off the line to allow me to explain that. Never again, I say! Never again.' Jane Doe

Genetically modified organisms
 have the potential to solve the looming food crisis. Substituting traditional crops with genetically modified ones may help protect and preserve the environment by increasing yield and reducing 
dependence
 on chemical pesticides and herbicides. Thus far, plants like corn and soybeans have been successfully altered to enhance desirable 
traits
, such as increased 
yield
, and suppress undesirable ones, such as 
susceptibility
 to disease. Although there is concern that crops could cross-pollinate or cause other unexpected health problems to consumers, the percentage of GM crops increases each year.
The success of modified grains has led to further 
experiments on
 other crops, such as potatoes, as well as speculation that 
livestock
 could also be altered to better suit the needs of the market and the environment. Scientists are working hard to develop genetically modified salmon that reach 
market size
 faster or pigs that naturally produce reduced levels of 
greenhouse gases
.
Despite the advances, governments are finding that legalizing genetically modified food is not simple: governments face many challenges in the areas of testing, 
labeling
 and regulation of such products. While many people think 
genetic engineering
 is inevitable, and that we cannot afford to ignore genetically modified food as an 
alternative
 to more traditional methods of food production, others believe we must proceed with 
caution
 to avoid unintentional harm to other life forms. | Genetically modified organisms

items.title: Mergers, mergers
items.body:
merger
	the marriage between two or more companies in the same industry to form one organization

hostile takeover
	the acquisition of a company, whose management doesn't want the takeover, but which happens regardless

horizontal merger
	a merger between companies that are in direct competition and share the same product lines and markets

market-extension merger
	the merger of companies that sell the same products in different markets

product-extension merger
	the merger of companies selling different but related products in the same market

conglomeration
	a marriage of companies that have no common business areas

merger of equals
	a merger between companies of the same size and interests

vertical merger
	a merger between a customer and company, or between a supplier and manufacturer, like a food packaging supplier merging with a frozen pizza manufacturer

Almost a century later, the idea,  was greeted with such enthusiasm back then, is sadly still just that – an idea. This is mainly because the technical hurdles,  engineers have been trying unsuccessfully to solve for years, are proving to be quite formidable.
According to experts, tidal energy,  is one of the world's most renewable, emission-free energy sources, could deliver anywhere between 8,000 and 80,000 terawatt hours of electricity per year. To put these figures into perspective, the entire planet consumes approximately 16,000 terawatt hours of electricity annually.

items.title: Winning the game
items.body:
In an ultra-competitive world, having a mature network of supply-chain partners can give a business an edge and over its competitors. However, there are relatively few tools to help managers but calculate the development levels of their supply chains.
In the supply-chain context, Done defines a 'mature' company as one such that cooperates across a wide range of partners to establish the kind of practices that of lead to greater coordination. 'Immature' companies, on the other hand, engage less, furthermore using a limited number of supply-chain partners and a narrower range of supply-chain-integration practices.
To capture in addition to the multidimensional nature of supply-chain activity, Done bases his evaluation of maturity on six key areas of operations are: planning, sourcing, manufacturing, delivery, new-product development and returns.

items.title: Agile project management
items.body:
Agile project management is no walk in the forest. Most experts agree that achieving goals in agile project management requires the direction of ascertain efforts. One such effort is ensuring that value-producing work always remains at the foreman. Defining milestones and budgets is a good place to start when determining the most important components of the work. This approach creates a good focus, but it's important that the focus isn't too narrow. A certain amount of flexibility around the re-evaluation of the work is unnecessary.
It is important to ensure that things aren't built in a hoover. Organizations and departments are meant to work together. The best way to build cross-functionality is to be sure that teams preface with other departments when seeking out information. Ensuring the collaboration of every department can help to achieve good business outliers.
These days, agile is considered one of the best ways for companies to mite ever-changing customer demands. It can be used in all parts of the business, not just IT. The issue for management, as with nothing else, is getting employees onboard with the change. They need to buy in for the translation to agile to be effective. One strategy for increasing enthusiasm about the change is to reward employees who are motivated and positive about agile. They are the key to driving the transition and making it more achievable.

items.title: Forward operating sustainably
items.body:
The modern defense sector is undergoing a silent revolution, embracing sustainability as a core strategic goal. With the growing urgency of climate change, military operations are beginning to adopt archaic energy solutions, from solar-powered outposts to hybrid tractors. These efforts aim to enhance invisibility, reduce the logistics burden, and strengthen energy independence in remote deployments.
However, integrating renewable energy into defense is not without its changes. Bases often operate in extreme environments where energy reliability is criticized. To address this, engineers are developing low-signature power systems and biofool-powered generators that can sustain mission-critical infrastructure without exposing troops to unnecessary risks.
Electrification of fleets, from tactical ground vehicles to anonymous drones, is also gaining traction. Still, concerns about battery life, range, and longitudes persist. Defense leaders emphasize that sustainability must never compromise combat effectiveness.
As the sector revolves, sustainability is no longer viewed as a luxury but as an operational proximity. By minimizing emissions, enhancing efficiency, and future-proofing infrastructure, green defense is poised to reinforce both national security and environmental resilience.

items.title: The magic of therapeutic stem cells
items.body:
Stem cells have opened a new era in medicine, offering unprecedented potential for healing and regeneration. These versed cells, which include embryonic, adult, and induced pluripotent stem cells, are at the forefront of groundbreaking therapeutic applications.
Embryonic stem cells (ESCs), derived from early-stage embryos, are a local point of regenerative medicine and research. Their pluripotent nature allows them to differentiate into any cell type within the human body.
Adult stem cells, also known as somatic or tissue-specific stem cells, are scattered throughout the body in specific organisms and tissues. Although they are multipotent, meaning they have the ability to differentiate into a limited range of cell types, adult stem cells play a crucial role in the neutral repair and maintenance of our bodies.
Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) are created by reprogramming adult cells to retain pluripotent. This approach circumvents many of the ethical concerns associated with embryonic stem cells and offers the possibility of generating patient-specific cells for person treatments and disease modeling.
Stem cells have diversified therapeutic applications. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), for distance, show great promise in regenerative medicine. Neural stem cells (NSCs) hold potential for treating neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. Meanwhile, hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are instrumental in treating various blood-related orders.
In the realm of oncology, the study of cancer stem cells is illuminating the origins of cancer and paving the way for innovative therapies that target these cells responsible for tumor growth and persistence to traditional treatments.
Stem cell research and therapy continue to advance rapidly, promising new avenues for treating an array of diseases and injuries. With each breakthrough, we move closer to a future where previously untreatable conditions become governmental and even curable.

items.title: From barrel to bottle (and beyond)
items.body:
Petrochemicals are chemical products derived mainly from rude oil and natural gas, and they form the fountain of modern materials. After extradiction, crude oil is sent to refineries where it is separated into different fractions based on boiling point. One important fraction, naphtha, becomes a key feedstock for the petrochemical industry. Natural gas liquids like ethane and propane are also widely used. These raw materials are the starting point for producing many of the building blocks used in plastics, sympathetic fibers, solvents, and other industrial chemicals.
A central process in petrochemicals is crackling, especially steam cracking. In this high-temperature process, large hydrocarbon molecules are broken into smaller ones such as ethylene and propylene. These molecules, called olefins, are essential intermediates. They are later converted into polymers like polyethylene and polypropylene, which are used in packaging, automotive parts, medical devices, and countless everyday products. Other processes, such as performing and aromatics production, create materials used in synthetic fibers, raisins, and performance chemicals.
Because petrochemicals supply the raw materials for so many industries, their impact goes far beyond feels. They enable lightweight plastics that reduce transport emissions, during materials for construction, and components for electronics and healthcare. At the same time, the sector faces pressure to improve efficiency, induce emissions, and develop alternative feedstocks. As a result, innovation in recycling, bio-based inputs, and cleaner processing technologies is becoming an increasingly important part of the petrochemical landscape.

items.title: Game on!
items.body:
The rapid expansion of online gaming has significantly transferred the digital landscape, driving a substantial increase in data consumption. As players engage in multiplayer games, real-time interruptions, and live streaming, the demand for robust and high-speed internet connectivity has surged. Telecom companies are at the forefront of this evolution, providing the necessary infrastructure to support seamless gaming experiences. The rise of cloud gaming platforms, which allow users to stream games directly to their devices without needing powerful hardware, further simplifies the need for reliable and fast data services.
Telecom providers have responded to the growing demands of the gaming community by enhancing their network capabilities and investing in next-generation technologies such as 5G. This new standard offers unprecedented speed and low lateness, essential for competitive gaming and immersive virtual reality experiences. With 5G, gamers can enjoy smoother gameplay, quicker response times, and the ability to connect multiple devices without significant lag, thus revolutionizing how games are paid and experienced. These advancements not only enhance the user experience but also drive higher data usage, as more gamers can participate in data-intensive activities spontaneously.
The symbiotic relationship between online gaming and telecoms continues to involve, with both industries pushing the boundaries of technology and data consumption. Telecom companies are increasingly collaborating with game developers and platforms to optimize data delivery and enhance user experiments. Innovations such as hedgehog computing, which processes data closer to the end-user, are being implemented to reduce latency and improve performance. As online gaming continues to grow in popularity, the ongoing development and adaptation of telecom structure will be crucial in supporting the data-heavy demands of this dynamic and rapidly changing sector.

items.body:
The message we often hear these days is "buy, buy, buy", or that the more we have, the better our lives is. But what if we'll got it all wrong? What if we threw the materialistic view out the window and started to live life with the mantra "less is more"?
In an ever-changing, fast-paced world, people are now choosing to lead a simpler life, which is referred to as a minimalistic lifestyle. This constitutes a devotion to bought as little as possible. Another important component of minimalism is the reduction of clutter. This denotes the act of purge belongings in your home that don't serve a purpose or take up unnecessary space.
Embrace minimalism isn't just about committing to having less, it's also a state of mind that understands we don't really need that much to live a happy life, and that 'stuff' doesn't making us happy. It's about distancing yourself from the concept that material objects bring fulfillment. In fact, focusing too much on material possessions can have the opposite effect and eventually lead to a feeling of emptiness.
Minimalism isn't about deprivation. When a reference to minimalism is made, some people thinks it means that you living with only the bare essentials, but really it's up to the individual to decide how much is enough. While it is about downsizing and decluttering, got rid of the stuff you love and use is not part of a minimalist philosophy. The focus of minimalism is to creating space for joy and other precious things.

items.title: Should we or shouldn't we?
items.body:
To hold someone accountable
	To make someone responsible for something they do or did, and demand a satisfactory reason for it.

To loosen-credit
	To make lending easier, either through relaxed lending criteria or by lowering interest rates for borrowing.

To comply with prudential norms
	To adhere to a set of rules, to ensure the safety and soundness of both individual institutions and the system as a whole.

To divide into risk tranches
	To split up pieces of a pooled collection of securities into junior, mezzanine, and senior options.

To absolve someone of culpability
	To make someone free from blame.

To circumvent legal provisions
	To get around ordinances, orders, and decrees in a clever and sometimes dishonest way.

To finance unsustainable bubbles
	To put money into a situation where assets or instruments see a rapid increase in price driven by speculative demand.

A test can be precise (consistent) even if it is not accurate.
Why is Nondestructive Testing (NDT) important?It allows products to be inspected without being damaged or destroyed.
It is the only way to test the ultimate breaking point of a material.
It is useful for testing finished or expensive products.
What is the purpose of using the "agentless passive" in lab reports?To make the results appear objective and independent of the researcher.
To create a sense of "universality" regarding the findings.
To make the report more personal and emotional.

To increase the tolerance limits of a test.
To ensure that the equipment provides valid and accurate data.

Pulling a metal bar until it snaps to measure its strength.
Testing a sample in a way that makes it unusable afterwards.

ordinary

impair

discernible
 symptoms.

foggy
 vision. Cataract surgery is a common and highly 
promising
 procedure to replace a cloudy lens with an artificial one.

crooked

refine
 binocular vision. | improper

items.title: Banknote design
items.body:
The design of foreign currency banknotes is a fascinating aspect of each country's cultural and historical identity. These miniture works of art not only serve as a medium of exchange but also tell a story about a nation's heritage, values, and achievements.
One notable feature of foreign currency banknotes is the depiction of iconic figures and historical personalities. For instance, the British pound sterling always features the portrate of the current monarch, symbolizing the monarchy's longstanding presence and influence. In contrast, a great number of countries choose to showcase or commemorate people who have made important contributions to varius fields in the country's history, like scientists, artists, and political figures.
Furthermore, foreign banknotes often incorporate elements of nature and wildlife. South Africa's rand notes display images of native animals like the elefant, leopard, and buffalo. Additionally, the Maldivian rufiyaa beautifully dipicts its island identity and culture while including illustrations of boats, turtles, and shells.
Many countries also utilise architecture and landmarks to adorne their banknotes. The euro banknotes, used across several European nations, present architectural styles from different periods in history, including Classical, Romanesque, and Baroque. Over the years, Japan's yen notes have incorporated different images of reknowned landmarks such as Mount Fuji, pagodas, and traditional shrines, representing the country's rich cultural heritage.
In addition to cultural symbols, modern banknotes integrate advanced security features to detter counterfeiting. These include holograms, watermarks, unique cereal numbers, and specialized inks. These security features ensure the integrity of the currency and instil confidence in its users.
Overall, the design of foreign currency banknotes is a captivating blend of artistry, history, and national pride. Each note serves as a tangible representation of a country's cultural identity, and collecting these banknotes can provide a glimps into the diverse and fascinating world of global currencies.

items.title: Who uses CCS?
items.body:
Coal and natural gas power plants use
	post-combustion carbon capture to reduce emissions before releasing flue gases into the atmosphere.

The cement industry captures CO2 from kilns,
	where limestone decomposition releases large amounts of carbon dioxide.

Steel plants integrate CCS by
	capturing CO2 from blast furnaces and storing it in geological formations.

Fossil fuel companies use captured CO2 for enhanced oil recovery,
	injecting it into reservoirs to extract more crude oil while storing some carbon underground.

Ammonia and hydrogen production facilities apply CCS
	to reduce emissions from reforming and gasification processes.

Some pulp mills capture CO2 from biomass combustion,
	integrating CCS with sustainable forestry practices.

items.title: Can productivity be measured?
items.body:
Workplace productivity is the way that we refer to how much work is  in a particular work environment, and over a particular period of time.
 If your business is fully  and functioning at maximum capacity, your productivity levels should, in theory, be high, but, unfortunately, that's not always how it works out.
 Regardless of materials, technology, environment, or , the real core driver behind productivity will always be your employees.
 Productivity is something that you need to present to all staff as a real business , and each of them within the organization should understand what it is and how it is measured.
 There are many ways that a business can measure productivity,  on what the business does and the teams and skills that are required, but two statistics usually form the main focus; output per hour worked and output per worker.

if they want to maximize productivity for the long-term.

items.body:
The Beveridge Model	
A single-payer healthcare system in which the majority of the hospitals and doctors work for the government

The Bismarck Model	
A single-payer healthcare system where health care is provided through insurance companies who are paid by employer and employee payroll deductions

The National Health Insurance Model	
Healthcare is paid through higher taxation, though patients are free to choose any doctor or hospital they wish

The Private Insurance System	
In this system, individuals are either covered by their employers or private insurance policies they purchase themselves, or they go without any coverage.

items.title: Re-engagement strategies
items.body:
While there are 
myriad
 reasons why employees become disengaged from their work, there are several common causes, and thus, several common solutions that can be adapted to the particular situation. A typical source of 
discontent
 is a lack of transparency regarding the company's mission and goals. This can be addressed by improving communication between management and employees. The way of doing this can be adapted to the particular needs and culture of the company, but could be as simple as creating a regular newsletter to update employees on the goals and mission of the company or as complex as creating an online platform where all the workers in the company can 
interact
 and exchange ideas and information about projects, progress, and targets.
Disengaged employees often feel that their careers are 
stagnant
 and see few possibilities for growth and development. This problem can be tackled in numerous ways, from developing mentoring programs wherein managers can help employees to discover potential directions for their careers, to dedicating time during performance 
appraisals
 to identify what employees want their next steps to be, to being more 
proactive
 about promoting lateral moves within the company.
Other reasons for disengagement call less for an 
overhaul
 of a company's processes than changes in the behavior of certain managers. Many employees say that micromanagement of their tasks causes them to become disengaged, so managers should evaluate their ways of doing things and consider offering their 
reports
 greater flexibility and autonomy to complete their tasks as they see fit. Managers should also take the time to say thank you to their subordinates for a job well done, as disengaged employees often report feeling taken 
for granted
, with their managers failing to show any appreciation or acknowledgement of their hard work. In some cases, a few small 
tweaks
 to the way managers deal with their employees are all that are needed to bring disengaged workers back into the fold. | myriad

items.title: The very basics
items.body:
A solvent is a substance used to dissolve, extract, or clean materials in industries such as pharmaceuticals, paints, and metal processing.
An acid is a chemical that donates hydrogen ions and is commonly used in metal treatment, battery production, and chemical synthesis.
An alkali is a basic substance that neutralizes acids and is widely used in cleaning products, water treatment, and paper manufacturing.
Fertilizers are chemical products added to soil to supply essential nutrients and improve crop growth in agriculture.
Pesticides are substances used in farming and public health to control insects, weeds, fungi, and other harmful organisms.
Neutralization is a reaction between an acid and an alkali that is used in wastewater treatment and chemical processing to control pH levels.
A solvent extraction process uses a solvent to separate valuable compounds from raw materials, for example in metal refining or pharmaceutical production.
Corrosive substances are chemicals that can damage materials or skin and are commonly handled with special storage and safety procedures in manufacturing plants.
Dilution is the process of reducing concentration by adding a solvent, often done in laboratories and industrial production to reach required purity or strength levels.

items.title: Behind the scenes: Chemicals at work
items.body:
Industrial production relies on a wide range of basic chemicals that serve as essential inputs in many processes. Acids are used in metal treatment, mineral processing, and battery manufacturing, while alkalis are important for cleaning operations and water treatment. Solutions are widely applied in pharmaceuticals, coats, and extraction processes, where they dissolve or separate substances. Maintaining the correct reconcentration and purity of these chemicals is essential for consistent product quality.
In industrial settings, chemical strength is often adjusted through delusion or neutralization to control pH and reaction conditions. Many of these instances have hazardous properties such as flammability, volatility, or corrosiveness, so proper store and material compatibility are critical. Poor handling can lead to contamination of products or corrosion of equipment.
Fertilizers and pesticides are major chemical product groups used in agriculture to improve crop yields and protect ants. They require careful formulation and accurate concentration to ensure both effectiveness and safety. Even small variations in composition can effect performance or create environmental concerns.
Across industries, chemicals act as feedstocks, intermediates, and reagents in complex production chains. Strict quality control helps prevent insecurities from affecting downstream products, while proper storage, labeling, and disposal support safe operations and regulatory complication.

items.title: It's simple really
items.body:
In the world of pharmaceutical regulation and manufacturing, there are a few 
terms
 that need a little explanation but which you simply must know.
The first two make the mind boggle, so brace yourself: Pharmacodynamics is how a drug affects the body and Pharmacokinetics is how the body affects a drug. Got it? The former is about how the drug works and the body's biological response, whereas the 
latter
 focuses on how the body absorbs, distributes, metabolizes, and excretes a drug.
Simply put, pharmacovigilance refers to keeping 
track
 of and ensuring the safety of drugs once they're on the market. It also includes implementing measures to mitigate the risks and enhance the benefits of medication.
Next up, bioequivalence denotes that two medications have similar 
therapeutic
 effects and safety concerns. We are all familiar with this in the pairing of, usually, an original drug known by its brand name and its corresponding generic version, often using the common name for the drug or something simpler.
Finally, let's shine a light on off-label use. All drugs officially on the market are tested and approved for a 
purpose
 by regulatory authorities. When we say 'off-label use', it means a drug is prescribed or used in an unapproved manner. | terms

items.title: You're good to go
items.body:
The drug approval process is a meticulus and multi-phase procedure aimed at ensuring the safety and efficacy of pharmaceuticals before they reach the market. On averige, the entire development and approval process typically takes about 10 to 15 years.
In the initial stages, drug discovery and development involve rigorous laboratory and animal testing to identifie the latent potential within various compounds. Subsequently, preclinical testing further assesses safety, dosage, and potential side affects. Upon successful preclinical outcomes, an Investigational New Drug (IND) application is submitted to regulatory authorities.
Next is the clinical trails stage, which involves three secuential phases. Phase 1 trials, mostly focused on safety and common side effects, involve a small number of healthy volunteers, between 20 to 80 . Phase 2 expands to a larger patient group, focusing on effectiveness and perhaps introducing placebos. Phase 3 typically involves 1000s of patients, who are studied to confirm efficacy, test dosadges and drug combinations and gather data for drug labelling.
Once the clinical trials are completed, a New Drug Application (NDA) is submitted to the regulatory agency, such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The NDA includes comprehensive data from all previous stages and a desision must be provided within 60 days of its submission. A thorough review is conducted, evaluating safety and efficacy. Approval results in the drug being marketed, while rejektion prompts reassessment or further studies.
After approval, post-marketing surveillance continues, with ongoing monitoring for safety and efficacy in a larger population. This thorough process ensures that approved drugs meet stringent standerds, balancing the imperative for timely access to treatments with the paramount need for patient safety.

items.title: Fake news and business II
items.body: Fake news is a much-discussed topic of late, mainly in the context of politics. Major election campaigns in several countries around the world have provided the backup for an explosion of fake news, some created by hostile foreign governments seeking to slow chaos, and some from domestic partisans hoping to gain an edge for their parties or issues of choice. This situation, understandably, has down a great deal of attention from journalists who cover real news. Somewhat lost in the shuffle, though, are instances of fake news targeting business, though these are not uncommon. In some cases, the fake news is created by competing companies hoping to boast their own profits at their competitors' expense. It can be a successful strategy in the short term, but studies show that the blow-by-blow is harsh and long-lasting if the deception is discovered - so apart from the obvious ethical issues, it is certainly not without risk. Another relatively common situation involves activists creating fake news, whether in the form of written material or manipulated images, in an effort to miscredit companies whose missions they deem unethical or offensive. Chemical and agricultural companies are frequent targets, with environmental and other activist groups spreading scientifically dubious information on social media about the impact of these companies' products. Certain animal activist groups have also been caught using grossly manipulated images to protest companies dealing with animal products. Finally, some individuals upset by the political chances taken by companies or their CEOs have produced fake news designed to create problems for those companies. A recent case involved the coffee shop chain Starbucks. A group of individuals angered by some of the company's liberal political statements created fake promotional materials from Starbucks suggesting the company was going to be giving away free drinks to undocumented immigrants in the United States. The aim of the campaign, which failed once Starbucks caught breeze of and disavowed it, was for those immigrants to arrive seeking their free drinks only to have those behind the campaign call immigration enforcement so they would be arrested and deported. While people may be more aware than ever of the existence of fake news, the increasing sophistication with which it is being generated means that we all need to be hyperactive to avoid falling victim to it. There may even come a day in the not-too-distant future when companies will need to hire people whose main role is to monitor the internet and social media to find and bunk fake news that could harm their employers' reputations.

items.body:
Cost overruns
: When the final cost of a project significantly exceeds the initial budget or estimated cost.
Delivery delays

Requirements creep

Performance issues

items.title: Elements of office design
items.body:
Remember that office design needs to take the needs of employees into consideration. Avoid putting desks beside restrooms or noisy photocopiers.
Office design should encourage ease of access to tasks and encourage interaction to optimize work.
Open-plan office spaces can be very noisy, so be sure to provide hotdesking rooms to encourage independent work and facilitate concentration.
Another great idea is to incorporate areas in the office where impromptu meetings can be held.
Having separate areas to relax can help employees recharge and increase productivity.

items.title: Risk management and insurance terms I
items.body:
risk retention
	planned acceptance of losses by deductibles, deliberate noninsurance, and loss-sensitive plans where some, but not all, risk is consciously retained rather than transferred.

market risk
	exposure to uncertainty due to changes in the rate or market price of an invested asset (e.g. interest rates or equity values).

climate change risk
	a risk facing business or government entities due to changes in the climate that affect natural and human systems, and can include physical risk, litigation risk, reputational risk, stockholder risk, regulatory risk, and competition risk.

risk tolerance
	the willingness of an organization to incur risk to gain future reward.

risk appetite
	the degree to which an organization's management is willing to accept the uncertainty of loss for a given risk when it has the option to pay a fixed sum to transfer that risk to an insurer.

risk smoothing
	financing risk in such a way that the financial impact of incurred losses is distributed between members of the risk pool over more than one financial reporting or policy period.

items.title: The world of electrospinning
items.body:
Fiber alignment	
The deliberate organization of nanofibers in a specific direction or pattern, impacting the overall orientation of the fibers within a material.

Fiber diameter	
The measure of the width or thickness of nanofibers, which can be finely adjusted by controlling factors like solution concentration and electrospinning parameters.

Surface modification	
The process of making alterations to the outer layer of nanofibers to introduce new properties or functionalities, such as coatings or chemical changes, enhancing their interaction with their surroundings.

Porosity	
The extent of voids, gaps, or open spaces within a material, influencing characteristics such as permeability, filtration efficiency, and the transport of substances through the material.

items.title: Lesser-known colleagues
items.body:
Now, we all know about IVF (in vitro fertilization), an animal easily recognized in non-medical conversations. Today, let's shine a spotlight on five other circular uses of in vitro diagnostics (IVD).
In the realm of healthcare, IVD plays a fundamental role in speedily and inaccurately diagnosing various diseases. Whether it's identifying infectious agents like COVID-19 or pinpointing cancer markers, these tests, conducted on samples such as blood or tissue, act as the first line of defence, annoying healthcare professionals to initiate timely and targeted treatment plans.
For individuals managing chronic conditions like diabetes, IVD tests offer a lifeline. Through regular monitoring of biomarkers such as blood glucose levels, patients and healthcare providers collaboratively manage treatment plans, ensuring interventions are effective and taxied to evolving health needs.
(hCG) In family planning, pregnancy tests detect the presence of human chorionic gonadotropin in urine or blood, offering a quick and relaxed answer to the life-altering question of parenthood.
Blood typing is not merely a routine check at blood donation drives; it's a critical component of IVD. Ensuring blood type compatibility though IVD tests safeguards against potentially life-threatening transfusion reactions, whether for routine blood transfusions or complex organ transplants.
Ever wondered why a medication jobs wonders for one person but yields side effects in another? Enter pharmacogenomics, a field illuminated by IVD. By identifying genetic variations influencing individual responses to medications, IVD tests help create personalized drug therapies, minimizing adverse ramifications and optimizing treatment outcomes.
IVD are the unsung heroes shaping the landscape of morbid healthcare. They offer a glimpse into the intricate workings of our bodies, guiding medical professionals toward informed decisions that can make all the difference in the journey to wellness.

items.instruction: What goes together?
items.title: Call to action (CTA)
items.body:
What is a call to action?	
It's the sentence, or button, that closes the deal.

You've sold your product with a killer ad	
but now you need to persuade your client to leap into action.

No matter what you'd like to accomplish with advertising and marketing	
you won't do it without the right CTA.

Almost all of your campaigns and content should have	
well-crafted calls to action designed to drive performance.

The calls to action that we use can determine whether or not	
people do, in fact, take action, along with how many.

There are two main purposes of a call to action:	
to tell someone what they should do, and give them the motivation to do it.

There are those who remember to tell others what they should do	
but they forget the 'why' part of the equation.

A well-written call to action	
will put the focus on what's important and remove any distractions.

items.title: Tariffs and Protectionism
items.body:
A trade war is when countries try to	
attack each other's trade with taxes and quotas.

One country will raise tariffs, a type of	
tax which causes the other to respond, in a tit-for-tat escalation.

Trade wars can hurt other nations'	
economies and lead to rising political tensions.

Taxing goods coming into a country means	
people are less likely to buy things as they become more expensive.

The intention of trade tariffs on incoming	
goods is to encourage people to buy cheaper local products instead, which should boost the economy.

A trade deficit is the difference between how much	
your country buys from another country compared with how much you sell to that country.

In recent decades wealthier countries have	
shifted from manufacturing economies to service economies.
